children: Graphite India shares saw profit booking in trade on Thursday after rising more than 17 per cent in the previous two sessions.
Shares of the company traded up to 1 per cent lower at Rs 838.50 apiece on the NSE, down 0.73 per cent.

The stock had gained more than 17 per cent in the previous two sessions. The sharp 15 per cent rise in the previous session came after global graphite electrode maker GrafTech International announced a 30 per cent price increase, raising expectations of firmer electrode prices globally.
The development gains significance as Graphite India is currently the only listed pure-play company in the space.

Prasenjit Paul, Fund Manager and Wealth & Research Analyst at Paul Asset, said higher electrode prices could meaningfully improve Graphite India's earnings, but GrafTech's 30 per cent hike does not automatically mean a similar increase for the company.
"The actual benefit depends on prices secured on new orders and renewals, and how input costs move," he said.

"There is a fundamental reason for the optimism, as better pricing can improve earnings, but the market is already anticipating some of that benefit. I would look for stronger order pricing and operating margins before calling the entire rally justified," Paul said.
He said the development showed producers were pushing for better prices, rather than demand having suddenly strengthened.
"The real test of pricing power is whether customers accept the increase without a meaningful drop in order volumes," he said.
Paul said other electrode producers could benefit, but the optimism should not be extended to all metal stocks.
"For steelmakers using electric arc furnaces, higher electrode prices could instead put pressure on margins unless they can pass on the additional cost," he said.

"I would track fresh order prices, sales volumes and input costs to see whether better pricing is actually reaching operating profit. Further upside will depend on how much earnings improve against what the share price already reflects," he added.

On the technical front, Virat Jagad, Senior Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza, said Graphite India had seen a bullish breakout above the horizontal resistance at Rs 800 on strong volume expansion.
"Look for a retest entry near Rs 800-810, keeping a stop loss below Rs 770 to limit risk. Initial target sits at Rs 920-950, with potential expansion towards Rs 1,000," he said.
Jagad added that the stock was trading well above its key moving averages, while the Relative Strength Index (RSI) had moved above 70, indicating strong momentum.
